authorization: User requested a bounded feasibility screen of reverse, bit-lane, and centre-out deterministic orders while other small decoding-order work proceeds. This is isolated research; it does not reopen closed composition work or resume the stopped broad benchmark.

inputs.note: The six source ranges exactly repeat DECODING-ORDER-1. The three compressed ranges exactly repeat the existing compressed-asset screen's frozen middle windows. The runner verifies the declared hashes before testing.

transforms: reverse the complete MSB-first bit sequence
centre-out bytes: c=floor((n-1)/2), then c,c+1,c-1,c+2,c-2,... while in range
global MSB-first bit lanes k=2,3,4; lane j contains positions j,j+k,...; final lane byte is zero padded
lane_transport: separate: each packed lane independently coded; all coded lengths are in the frame
concatenated: packed lanes concatenated before one coder stream; lane raw lengths derive from original bit length and k
frame: DLV1 | original_length:u32be | transform:u8 | codec:u8 | stream_count:u8 | repeated coded_length:u32be,coded_stream. Transform and codec tags are charged. The frame is self-contained; no input-specific order, permutation, or selector is transmitted.
controls: Identity uses the same DLV1 wrapper and each coder. Report deltas versus same-coder identity and the smaller identity wrapper. The per-sample best transform is an outcome oracle unless a future encoder selection rule and its cost are specified; it is reported as diagnostic only.
validation: For every byte length 0 through 17, test deterministic transforms and complete frames with both coders. Verify lane padding is zero and all inverse transforms restore byte-exactly. On real samples save one best physical frame per coder, reconstruct it in a fresh Python process using the frame alone, and compare SHA-256.
scope_limit: A 9-window, 4 KiB fixed screen. It is not a CIX archive result, not broad qualification, and does not establish a production selector. A result neither revives nor refutes earlier lane/transform work outside these exact finite variants.
failure_policy: Preserve errors; no outcome-driven transform, coder, source, or parameter changes.
